title: REQ-03-02 Indicator 2 'Days with delay': option list + daysWithDelayWl
context:
Why: Indicator 2 (Ind. 2) of the Watchlist POC maps a dropdown option to a Watchlist level (WL 0-4, higher is worse). This slice is the pure mapping only; no UI, no I/O. Read CLAUDE.md first: plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs), no npm dependencies (do not touch package.json), tests with node:test + node:assert/strict, pure functions, no I/O in src/indicators (no fs/net/process.env/console).

Files (create; src/indicators and test/indicators do not exist yet): src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs and its unit tests test/indicators/daysWithDelay.test.mjs. Work TDD (tests first). Do NOT create or edit anything under test/integration (QA owns test/integration/indicators/daysWithDelay.int.test.mjs). Do NOT touch src/indicators/delayCount.mjs (parallel card B2); the module must not import it or any other module and must share no state.

Exact exports (names are contract):
- `export const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS = Object.freeze(['no delay', '<=3 days', '>3 days', '>60 days', '>90 days'])` - exactly these 5 strings, this order, frozen (X-option-immutability).
- `export function daysWithDelayWl(option)` -> 0 | 2 | 3 | 4. Mapping: 'no delay' -> 0; '<=3 days' -> 0; '>3 days' -> 2; '>60 days' -> 3; '>90 days' -> 4. Resulting values for the options in order: [0, 0, 2, 3, 4].

Input handling (X-trim-whitespace): if typeof option !== 'string' throw RangeError (no coercion; `new String('>3 days')`, arrays, numbers, null, undefined, and no argument all throw). Otherwise apply String.prototype.trim() and match EXACTLY, case-sensitively, against the five options. Internal spacing is NOT normalised ('> 3 days' throws). Empty / whitespace-only strings trim to '' and throw. Return the WL number only, never the trimmed string.

Security (NFR-security): do not look up via a plain object keyed by the input, because 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__', 'hasOwnProperty', 'length' would hit inherited properties. Use a Map, a switch, or array indexOf on the frozen list; those strings must throw RangeError.

Errors (X-errors-message): throw `new RangeError(...)`. Message text is free (suggested: include the offending value, formatted safely so building the message never throws a non-RangeError for the listed inputs). Tests assert only `assert.throws(fn, RangeError)`, never the message.

Unit tests to write must cover: option list deepStrictEqual + Object.isFrozen; each option -> WL and the in-order [0,0,2,3,4] check over DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS; trimming (`'  >3 days '`->2, `'\t>60 days\n'`->3, `' no delay'`->0); invalid strings throwing RangeError: '', '   ', '>3 Days', 'No delay', '> 3 days', '>3days', '≤3 days' (Unicode <=), '>30 days', '>=3 days', '3 days', '>120 days', '0', '>1'; non-strings throwing RangeError: undefined, null, 0, 3, true, [], ['>3 days'], {}, new String('>3 days'), and a call with no argument; inherited names 'constructor','toString','__proto__','hasOwnProperty','length' throw RangeError; idempotence (same input -> same output repeatedly) and that the options array is still frozen with the same content after calls.
acceptance: AC-1: DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS deep-strictly equals ['no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days'] (5 strings, this order) and Object.isFrozen is true
AC-2: daysWithDelayWl('no delay') === 0 and daysWithDelayWl('<=3 days') === 0
AC-3: daysWithDelayWl('>3 days') === 2
AC-4: daysWithDelayWl('>60 days') === 3
AC-5: daysWithDelayWl('>90 days') === 4
AC-6: for every entry of DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS the call does not throw and the in-order results are [0,0,2,3,4]
AC-12: '  >3 days ' -> 2, '\t>60 days\n' -> 3, ' no delay' -> 0 (trimmed, WL only returned)
AC-14: each of '', '   ', '>3 Days', 'No delay', '> 3 days', '>3days', '≤3 days', '>30 days', '>=3 days', '3 days', '>120 days', '0', '>1' throws RangeError
AC-16: undefined, null, 0, 3, true, [], ['>3 days'], {}, new String('>3 days'), and a call with no argument throw RangeError (no coercion)
AC-18: 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__', 'hasOwnProperty', 'length' throw RangeError (never a non-WL value or undefined)
AC-19 (this module): exports exactly DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS and daysWithDelayWl as ESM; no dependencies added to package.json; source performs no I/O (no fs/net/process.env/console)

AC-20 (this module): repeated calls with the same input return the same value; the options array stays frozen with unchanged content; the module imports no other module and shares no state with delayCount
